title.title: Lech's conjecture: multiplicity never drops along a flat map
title.subtitle: Claim: for every flat local map $R \to S$ of Noetherian local rings, $e(R) \le e(S)$

plain: A measure of how 'pinched' a point is can never drop when you pass along a flat map

beats.text: Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity measures how singular a local ring is
Lech proved dimension at most 2; Ma did dimension 3 in equal characteristic
The claim: every dimension and characteristic

steps: Reduce from every characteristic to characteristic $p$
Cohen factorizations carry it back: $e(R) \le e(S)$

achievement.label: Lech's conjecture (1960)
statement: R \to S \text{ flat local} \;\Longrightarrow\; e(R) \le e(S)
achievement.context: Before: dimension at most 2 (Lech, 1960) and dimension 3 in equal characteristic (Ma, 2017)
achievement.note: No restriction on residue fields; the paper is 41 pages

verify.detail: Lean has only a char-$p$ lemma comparing Dutta and Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities, not the theorem
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Multiplicity measures how singular a local ring is; Lech said flat maps never lower it.
Work in characteristic p with Frobenius-based multiplicities, then carry the result back.
Claimed: proved in every dimension and characteristic.

sources.quote: Lech conjectured in 1960 that Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity cannot drop along a flat local map: $e(R)\le e(S)$. He proved it in dimension at most 2.
Family 194 claims every dimension and characteristic, with no restriction on residue fields.
Lean covers only a supporting characteristic-$p$ lemma comparing Dutta and Hilbert–Samuel multiplicities over a complete domain
